correctionAndBoundaryPassages.text:
Every current /3 project carries CONTRACT_PROFILE_ID = closed-loop-completion-profile/1. A /3 project lacking that exact profile is pre-profile legacy data and cannot satisfy current gates. Migration either deterministically creates every required current-profile record and field with auditable receipts and valid provenance or preserves the project as historical and non-gating. Merely setting CONTRACT_PROFILE_ID without satisfying the profile validator is rejected.

Migration defaults cannot fabricate semantic review, human authority, execution, evidence, freshness, independence, backup custody, mobile acceptance, or delivery. Any such missing release-bearing fact remains UNKNOWN or incomplete. Contract-profile migration is idempotent and is covered by invalid legacy fixtures.

13.2 Registry-version migration

Every persisted reference to a field contract, stage operation, scope matrix, Test IR language or operation registry, parser or selector registry, canonicalization contract, ID contract, filename contract, date/time contract, handoff container, normalizer, or derivation is version-bound. Import or migration must either prove compatibility under an explicit migration rule or invalidate and regenerate the affected current work. Equal high-level schema names do not imply registry compatibility.

Required proof order:
syntax
→ authoritative field, operation, scope, durable-object, normalizer, derivation, and ID registries
→ contract-profile migration
→ Stage 01 raw-intake, unitization, human-authority, and semantic-challenge tests
→ Stage 02 bounded-search and Stage 03 omission-challenge tests
→ Stage 04 obligation and challenge tests
→ Test IR language, dataflow, registry, parser, and security tests
→ deterministic runtime
→ file-first response ingestion and attachment-slot tests
→ workflow, due-stage, evidence, release, and terminal gates
→ prompt semantics, prompt-file identity, disclosure, and leakage tests
→ full-cycle and isolated mutation verification
→ local Chromium
→ deploy
→ exact deployed-origin and deployed-byte verification
→ deployed Chromium
→ actual physical iPhone Safari acceptance
→ final acceptance publication
→ release tag

The minimum required target-identity tuple is: the physical-device human observation; reported iOS version; observed Safari user-agent string; viewport dimensions and device-pixel ratio; exact deployed commit and deployment-manifest digest; origin; and test-project identity. WebKit build identity and exact hardware model may remain UNKNOWN without blocking; every other tuple member is required.

The evidence file reaches CI through the repository as a committed file or authenticated workflow input from a submitter recorded in the acceptance artifact. Each MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE is single-use: CI accepts at most one evidence file per challenge and rejects reused, unknown, or expired challenges and any evidence bound to a different commit, manifest, origin, target, or test project; a superseding run requires a new challenge. The gate minimum for the physical-device fact is HUMAN_OBSERVATION by the recorded performer at the recorded identity assurance; that basis is explicitly sufficient and is never relabeled application-proven.
The repository-only specification and normative-requirement manifests remain CI evidence. They are not copied into ordinary runtime project state or external project prompts.
